security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, TypeScript examples, placeholder URLs, and safe environment-variable guidance. The only confirmed issue is the global npm install command in SKILL.md, which can modify the user environment and needs approval. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user approval before running global npm installs, and prefer project-local or npx commands when possible.

content.value_statement: Genkit setup and API changes can slow AI application work. This skill gives focused JS guidance, examples, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides Genkit setup for Node.js and TypeScript projects.
Shows current Genkit flow and generation patterns.
Explains common v1.x migration errors and fixes.
Documents Genkit CLI commands for docs, flows, and evaluation.
Provides examples for structured output, streaming, images, and speech.
limitations: Does not replace current official Genkit documentation.
Requires user approval before running install or dev server commands.
Uses Google AI examples by default unless another provider is requested.
Does not guarantee provider model names remain current.

use_cases.title: Start a Genkit Project
use_cases.description: Set up a minimal Genkit structure in an existing JavaScript or TypeScript codebase.

use_cases.title: Fix Genkit Migration Errors
use_cases.description: Identify deprecated imports, response access mistakes, and schema problems during Genkit v1.x upgrades.

use_cases.title: Add AI Media Features
use_cases.description: Use Genkit examples for streaming, image generation, speech generation, and provider-specific configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Genkit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Genkit in this TypeScript project. Check the current structure first, then add the smallest working configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Genkit flow for [task]. Use the existing provider if one is configured, and explain the files you changed.

prompt_templates.title: Debug an Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug this Genkit error: [paste error]. Check the common error patterns first, then propose the smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a larger provider-aware Genkit system
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a provider-aware Genkit architecture for [app]. Include flow boundaries, tool registration, validation schemas, and verification commands.

output_examples.input: Set up Genkit for a new Next.js app.
output: Detects the framework and existing Genkit packages.
Recommends the provider plugin and minimal AI folder layout.
Adds a Developer UI script for later user-approved testing.

output_examples.output: The response identifies incorrect Zod imports, recommends importing validation helpers from Genkit, and explains how to verify the fix.
The response explains model choice, required response modalities, media handling, and provider documentation checks.

best_practices: Verify Genkit API details with bundled references or the Genkit CLI before changing code.
Prefer project-local CLI commands and ask before installing global packages.
Keep flows, tools, and schemas small enough to test independently.
anti_patterns: Using deprecated pre-1.0 imports without checking the migration notes.
Running package installs or dev servers without user approval.
Hardcoding API keys instead of using environment variables.

faq.question: Does this skill install Genkit automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and may suggest commands that need user approval.

faq.question: Which language does it support best?
faq.answer: It focuses on JavaScript and TypeScript Genkit projects running on Node.js.

faq.question: Can it help with Genkit v1.x migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common deprecated imports, response access changes, and schema fixes.

faq.question: Does it support providers beyond Google AI?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to look up provider plugins and adapt examples.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready flows?
faq.answer: It can draft and refine flows, but users must review credentials, errors, and deployment settings.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Some suggested documentation lookups or package installs may use the network with user approval.
